admitted_primary_source.title: Boundary Problems for Wave Equations With Grazing and Gliding Rays
admitted_primary_source.reading_route: Author-hosted freely accessible PDF, read as extracted text; no source copy distributed.
admitted_primary_source.receiving_changes: Independent full operator product rule, ordered matrix transport, every boundary jet, classical amplitude summation, normalized smooth kernel remainder and exact conormal row.

source_correspondence: A0 retains all scalar principal coefficients, arbitrary complex matrix lower coefficients, the actual physical side and the proved boundary phase.
A1 is derived entry by entry and independently checked with variable coefficients and noncommuting matrices. The sign in L2, i h A prime convention, Q h term and recursion sign are retained.
A2 and A3 prove the smooth signed root, Hamilton derivative and ordered lift with a=g-s h, together with the full converse fold descent.
A4 converts the actual boundary odd coordinate with every radial power and applies both complete matrix parity theorems with the permitted normalization.

A5 through A7 fix the entire boundary value and solve every normal jet using the explicit scalar block inverse. Each correction is flat in v, its divisions have polynomial loss, and supported Borel realization preserves the attained solution.
A8 sums all amplitude orders on the fixed geometry and proves the precise classical remainders. Base differentiation commutes with the frequency cutoffs; every order cancels with the correct sign.

A9 proves the double Taylor factor q^L times |v|^K after every derivative. A10 combines it with differentiated global zero-free Airy bounds and the explicit exponential difference to gain any negative frequency power.

A11 defines the local kernel through test Fourier decay proved by integration by parts and establishes its smooth PDE remainder up to the actual boundary. Output localization error is retained explicitly.

A12 proves both exact trace rows, preserves the arbitrary complex conormal matrix, and identifies the leading orders and invertibility. It does not assert extension to the original weak energy domain or uniqueness.
The affine and ordered matrix gauge examples have exactly zero differential-equation error. The finite-power example supplies the exact maximum used in the illustrated bound.
Seventeen local nodes connect to 438 earlier entries in sixteen maps. The 102 external human proof dependencies are preserved; internal export closure and full strict propagation are not asserted.
